name: LinkedIn
summary: Only three permissions are open to everyone: sign-in (openid/profile/email) and posting as the member (w_member_social). Everything else an agent typically wants - company pages, ads, sales, recruiting data - sits behind partner programmes that LinkedIn must approve, and approval is not guaranteed.
difficulty_reason: Most useful data requires partner approval with no published timeline or guarantee; even the app itself must be verified by a LinkedIn Page super admin.

effort.hands_on: 30-60 min for an app with open permissions; days of paperwork for partner applications
effort.production: Same day for open permissions; weeks to months - or never - for partner programmes
effort.waiting_on: Page super-admin verification of the app (up to 30 days to act), then LinkedIn's partner-programme decisions.

bottom_line: Scope your agent to what is open: sign-in, reading the member's basic profile, and posting on their behalf. If your roadmap needs more (company pages, ads, Sales Navigator, Talent), apply now, in parallel with building, and have a product plan that works without it. Associate the app with your real company Page and get it verified on day one - partner applications depend on it.
app_type: LinkedIn Developer app (linkedin.com/developers/apps), associated with and verified by a LinkedIn Company Page; products added from the Products tab.

prerequisites.detail: Apps must be associated with a Page; a Page super admin verifies the association.
No fragments (#); query parameters are ignored.

stages.name: Create and verify the app
stages.goal: A verified app with client credentials.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Name, company Page, privacy policy URL, logo.

steps.title: Get the Page association verified
steps.detail: Settings > Verify > Generate URL; send it to the Page super admin, who has 30 days to approve. A denial invalidates all generated links.

steps.title: Add self-serve products
steps.detail: Products tab: 'Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' and 'Share on LinkedIn'.

stages.name: Wire up and test
stages.goal: Members can sign in and the agent can post for them.

steps.title: Add redirect URLs on the Auth tab
Implement the 3-legged flow
steps.detail: Code expires in 30 minutes; access tokens last 60 days. No programmatic refresh unless LinkedIn enables it for you - plan a re-consent prompt before expiry.

stages.name: Apply for gated access (if needed)
stages.goal: Decision from LinkedIn on partner products.

steps.title: Draft the application
steps.detail: Agent drafts use case, data handling and member-value narrative; you review for accuracy.

steps.title: Submit via Products tab or partner programme site
steps.detail: Advertising API via Products tab; SNAP and Talent via partner pages.

steps.title: Wait for LinkedIn's decision
steps.duration: Unpublished - plan for weeks to months

token_facts.value: Only for a limited set of approved partners
Invalidates all previous access tokens for that member

gotchas.title: No refresh tokens for most apps
gotchas.detail: Agents holding long-lived connections must re-prompt members roughly every 60 days. Re-auth is silent only if the member is still logged in and the token hasn't expired.

gotchas.title: Scope change kills existing tokens
gotchas.detail: Requesting a different scope set invalidates the member's earlier tokens - roll out scope changes deliberately.

gotchas.title: Approval is discretionary
gotchas.detail: Partner programmes are not a queue you can wait out. Build value on the open permissions first.

gotchas.title: Old scope names in tutorials
gotchas.detail: r_liteprofile / r_emailaddress are legacy; use openid, profile, email.

blockers.cause: The scope belongs to a product your app doesn't have.
blockers.next_step: Add the self-serve product, or apply for the gated product.

blockers.cause: App not verified by the Company Page super admin.
blockers.next_step: Regenerate the verification URL and get the super admin to approve within 30 days.

blockers.cause: Access token expiry without programmatic refresh.
blockers.next_step: Schedule a re-consent prompt before day 60.

agent_can: Tell you which of your features fit open permissions
Write the OIDC sign-in and posting flow
Probe the authorise endpoint for client/redirect errors
you_must: Own the LinkedIn Company Page and get the app verified by its super admin
Submit partner applications as the legal business

claims.claim: Open (self-serve) permissions are only profile, email (Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect) and w_member_social (Share on LinkedIn); most others require approval.
Compliance permissions are closed and cannot be requested.
Access tokens are issued with a 60-day lifespan; programmatic refresh tokens only for a limited set of partners; auth codes live 30 minutes.
Redirect URLs must be absolute, cannot contain '#', and query parameters are ignored.
App must be verified by a Page super admin, who has 30 days to use the URL; a denial invalidates all links.
claims.note: Taken from LinkedIn Help as surfaced by search 2026-11-03; page not fetched directly.

claims.claim: An unknown client_id is rejected on the authorise page with 'client_id is invalid'.
claims.note: Probe returned HTTP 200 'Authorize | LinkedIn' page containing the error text.

claims.claim: LinkedIn's OIDC discovery lists only openid/profile/email scopes and does not advertise PKCE.
claims.note: Fetched live 2026-11-03. Absence from discovery doesn't prove PKCE is unsupported for all app types.

open_questions: Approval timelines for Community Management and Advertising APIs are not published.
Whether a placeholder Company Page is acceptable for partner applications is reported by third parties but not confirmed by LinkedIn.
